_comment: Short 12 in docs/CONTENT.md: the claim. Linked from the app's 'What's an EOB?' box, which says an EOB is sent 'after processing a claim' and tells people to look under Claims on their insurer's site.
_injury: Walked into a glass door. Very clean glass. The bump is the reason for the visit, and the joke is the second sentence.
_order: The story runs down the board in the order the paper moves: doctor, claim, insurance, EOB, bill. 'The order it is meant to go in' is deliberate: Short 4 is about the bill arriving before the answer does.
_jargon: Never calls the bill 'the claim' (see docs/CONTENT.md): the claim is what the office sends the insurer, and the EOB is the insurer's answer to it.

variants.door: You walked into a glass door. Very clean glass. So you see your doctor.

body.text: That one visit makes three pieces of paper, and you only ever get two.
The first is the claim. Your doctor's office sends it to your insurance, not to you.
It lists what they did, in codes, and what they charge for each.
Your insurance answers it with the Explanation of Benefits. What they paid, and what is yours.
Then the bill comes to you, for your part.
Claim, answer, bill. That is the order it is meant to go in. And your insurer's website lists every claim, under Claims.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
